readAloud: Comments about appearance can affect confidence long after a conversation ends, especially when they come from someone close. A person who has experienced criticism may begin to expect rejection or compare every new relationship with a painful one from the past. Supportive partners can help by listening, showing affection, and avoiding jokes or comments that increase insecurity. However, lasting confidence usually cannot depend entirely on another person’s approval. It may also grow through self-care, positive friendships, realistic ideas about bodies, and activities that create a sense of competence. A healthy relationship should make both people feel respected as complete individuals. Reassurance matters most when it is combined with consistent behavior, honest communication, and space for each person to develop self-respect.
narrator: Imagine that a health organization is studying confidence and emotional support. You have agreed to participate in a telephone interview about body image and relationships.
questions: What kinds of experiences can influence a person’s body confidence?
If a friend feels unattractive after criticism, how would you support that person?
What behaviors help partners create emotional safety in a relationship?
Is reassurance from other people enough to build lasting self-confidence? Explain.
